author: DPA
title: Czech voters head to local and Senate polls in first test for Babiš - NewsBreak
text:
1 hours ago
FILE PHOTO - Czech Republic's Prime Minister Andrej Babis speaks during a press conference ahead of a meeting on economic and scientific diplomacy. (is associated with: «Czech voters head to local and Senate polls in first test for Babiš») Šimánek Vít/CTK/dpa The Czech Republic is holding two-day local and Senate elections from Friday, in the first test of public sentiment for the government of populist billionaire Andrej Babiš, which took office in December.
Polling stations open at 2 pm (1200 GMT), with voters also able to cast their ballots on Saturday.
More than 8 million eligible voters are being asked to elect municipal and town councils in more than 6,200 districts. In the country's major cities, housing shortages were a central issue during the campaign.
One-third of the seats in the Senate, parliament's upper house, are also being contested, as they are every two years. The vote will determine whether the liberal and conservative opposition can retain its majority in the chamber or whether the governing parties and their allies can make gains.
President Petr Pavel attracted attention ahead of the vote by announcing he would be unable to vote due to a private holiday outside the European Union.
Pavel would otherwise have been able to vote for the municipal council in his home village of Černoučky in the north-west of the country, which has just under 330 residents.
"The president regrets the planning error," his spokesman said. Postal voting is not available in Czech local elections.
